text: Which of the following describes the time complexity of Binary Search in the worst case?
explanation: Binary Search has a time complexity of O(log n) in the worst case, as it repeatedly halves the search space.

text: Which of the following search algorithms requires the array to be sorted?
explanation: Binary Search requires a sorted array to efficiently search for an element by dividing the search space in half.

text: What is the time complexity of a Linear Search algorithm?
explanation: Linear Search has a time complexity of O(n) as it checks each element in the array sequentially.

text: What is the best-case time complexity of Binary Search?
explanation: The best-case time complexity of Binary Search is O(1), which happens when the target element is found at the mid position on the first comparison.

text: What is the time complexity of the worst-case scenario for Linear Search?
explanation: In the worst case, Linear Search will check every element in the array, making its time complexity O(n).

text: Which of the following is true for the time complexity of Quick Sort in the worst case?
explanation: In the worst case, Quick Sort has a time complexity of O(n^2), which occurs when the pivot always divides the array into uneven parts.

text: In which case would the Linear Search be preferred over Binary Search?

choices.label: C
choices.text: When the array is very large

choices.label: D
choices.text: When searching for the maximum element

explanation: Linear Search is preferred when the array is unsorted, as Binary Search requires the array to be sorted.

text: What is the space complexity of the Binary Search algorithm?
explanation: The space complexity of Binary Search is O(1) for the iterative version, as it only uses a constant amount of extra space.

text: Which of the following is the correct order of Big O notations from slowest to fastest (most efficient)?

choices.label: A
choices.text: O(n log n), O(n^2), O(1), O(n)

choices.label: B
choices.text: O(n^2), O(n log n), O(n), O(1)

choices.label: C
choices.text: O(n), O(n log n), O(1), O(n^2)

choices.label: D
choices.text: O(1), O(n), O(n log n), O(n^2)

explanation: The order of Big O notations from fastest (least time complexity) to slowest (highest time complexity) is as follows: O(1) is constant time, O(n) is linear time, O(n log n) is log-linear time, and O(n^2) is quadratic time.
